title: Idempotency-Key required on money-moving endpoints
decision: Every endpoint that moves money must require an Idempotency-Key header, and retries must reuse the same key.
rationale: Settlement job failures last week were caused by retries without idempotency keys.
quote: Decision: every endpoint that moves money must require an Idempotency-Key header, and retries must reuse the same key.

title: No new microservices until ledger has full transfer test coverage
decision: No new microservices until the ledger monolith has full test coverage on transfers; new features go into the existing ledger service.
alternativesRejected: Splitting the ledger service into new microservices (debated, not adopted for now)
rationale: The page does not state a rationale for this decision.
revisitWhen: The ledger monolith has full test coverage on transfers.
quote: Decision: no new microservices until the ledger monolith has full test coverage on transfers; new features go into the existing ledger service.

title: Frontend server state: TanStack Query
decision: New frontend code uses TanStack Query for server state.
alternativesRejected: Redux for server state (superseded; must not be added to new screens)
rationale: The page does not state a rationale.
exceptions: Existing Redux slices are not removed wholesale; they are migrated when touched.
quote: New frontend code uses TanStack Query for server state. Redux is superseded and must not be added to new screens; existing Redux slices are migrated when touched.
pageTitle: ADR-005: Frontend server state with TanStack Query

title: Authentication through Auth0 (OIDC)
decision: All user sign-in goes through Auth0 using OIDC.
alternativesRejected: Storing passwords in our own database
Building our own login, password reset, or MFA flows
rationale: SOC 2 scope is smaller when credentials never touch our database, and Auth0 already provides MFA.
quote: All user sign-in goes through Auth0 using OIDC. We will not store passwords or build our own login, password reset or MFA flows.

title: Public partner API style: REST with OpenAPI 3.1
decision: The public partner API is REST described by an OpenAPI 3.1 spec, versioned in the URL (/v1/).
rationale: Per-field authorization and query cost limits are hard to audit for a regulated payments API.
exceptions: Internal tools may use whatever fits, but anything partners call must be in the OpenAPI spec.
quote: The public partner API is REST described by an OpenAPI 3.1 spec, versioned in the URL (/v1/). We decided not to offer GraphQL to partners, because per-field authorization and query cost limits are hard to audit for a regulated payments API.
pageTitle: ADR-003: Public partner API is REST with OpenAPI

title: Asynchronous jobs: Amazon SQS, not Kafka
decision: We use Amazon SQS queues for asynchronous work.
rationale: Running and upgrading a Kafka cluster is more operational load than a six-person team can carry, and event replay is not needed today.
revisitWhen: Revisit if we need ordered event replay across services or exceed 5,000 messages per second.
quote: We use Amazon SQS queues for asynchronous work. Kafka was rejected: running and upgrading a Kafka cluster is more operational load than a six-person team can carry, and we do not need event replay today.
pageTitle: ADR-002: Use SQS for asynchronous jobs, not Kafka

title: System of record: PostgreSQL
decision: PostgreSQL is the single system of record for all ledger and account data.
alternativesRejected: MongoDB (document database) for ledger, transaction or account data
Any other document database for ledger, transaction or account data
rationale: Every transfer must commit multiple entries together, and finance needs ad-hoc reporting with joins across accounts, entries and settlements. MongoDB was rejected for slower multi-document transactions, no team operational experience, and loss of strict constraints on money data; DynamoDB was rejected because reporting would need a separate analytics copy.
exceptions: Flexible metadata may be stored in a JSONB column instead of a new database.
quote: We use PostgreSQL as the single system of record for all ledger and account data. We will not introduce MongoDB or any other document database for ledger, transaction or account data.
pageTitle: ADR-001: PostgreSQL as the system of record

title: Schema changes via Alembic migrations
decision: Schema changes to the PostgreSQL database go through Alembic migrations.
rationale: Consequence of adopting PostgreSQL as the system of record; the page states schema changes go through Alembic migrations.
quote: Schema changes go through Alembic migrations.
pageTitle: ADR-001: PostgreSQL as the system of record
